db_evidence.notes: The memory DB has explicit, unambiguous evidence at exactly the clue interval: episodes:30sec:002293 (68790-68820) captions the player opening the elixir/inventory screen and drinking '上清金葫芦' (restores 5% max health); semantic_triples row 0001118 (snapshot_s=68820) records 'player character consumes 上清金葫芦 (restores 5% max health)', and row 0001117 (snapshot_s=68730) records 'player character upgrades 药王葫芦 via 直接饮用'. Critically, semantic_triples row 0000035 (snapshot_s=1950, much earlier in the game) establishes that this game's equipment system explicitly lists 头冠, 衣甲, 背甲, 臂甲, 腿甲, 护手, 铃儿, 葫芦 (headgear, robe, back-armor, arm-armor, leg-armor, gloves, bell, GOURD) as equipment slots -- i.e. the gourd genuinely is one of the game's 'equipment' slots, not merely a consumable, which is why the reference answer treats a gourd change as 'the most noticeable equipment upgrade'. All 5 rollouts' SQL queries covered the 68700-69300ish window and thus pulled this gourd text into context, but none surfaced it as an equipment answer.

root_causes: Systematic framing bias: every rollout implicitly narrowed 'equipment' to weapon/armor/headgear and phrased every clip_qa question around those three categories, so even when the golden-gourd consumption text was sitting in the SQL results they had already pulled, none of them asked the visual sub-agent about the gourd/potion equipment slot.

The agents did not use the domain fact (established earlier in the same DB, semantic_triples row 0000035) that the equipment menu itself explicitly enumerates 葫芦 (gourd) as one of its slots alongside headgear/armor -- they never queried or noticed that fact, so they had no prior reason to treat a gourd change as 'equipment'.

Rollout 3 additionally missed the exact clue window in its visual check (clip_qa at 69060-69180 vs the true clue interval 68811-68825), landing on an unrelated scene and producing an unrelated wrong answer ('金棕衣').

Visually, weapon/armor/mask changes are more salient and easier for a frame-sampling clip_qa call to describe than a small gourd icon swap inside a menu list, biasing the visual sub-agent's free-form descriptions toward weapon/armor even when asked more broadly.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly located the general clue time window via SQL/semantic_search over episodes/visual_clips/event_steps around both the first and second Yin Tiger challenges -- retrieval of the relevant time window was not the bottleneck for 4 of 5 rollouts.
All rollouts appropriately escalated to clip_qa to visually verify equipment differences between the two encounters, following the intended tool workflow.
transferable_lessons: For 'equipment upgrade' questions in this game's memory DB, do not assume 'equipment' means only weapon/armor/headgear -- check the DB's own equipment-slot enumeration (e.g. semantic_triples rows describing the equipment menu's slot list) before restricting the visual sub-agent's question scope.

When run_sql or semantic_search returns episode/visual_clip captions that explicitly name an item (here '上清金葫芦'/'葫芦'), that literal keyword match should be weighed at least as heavily as a subjective visual weapon/armor comparison -- don't let a later clip_qa call silently override strong direct textual evidence already in context.

When asking clip_qa to compare two time windows for 'what changed', keep the question maximally open ('list every visible change in the full equipment/inventory screen including consumables/gourd/talismans') rather than pre-naming candidate categories (weapon, armor, headgear), since pre-naming categories biases the sub-agent's answer toward those categories and away from anything else in frame.
Verify the exact clue-interval seconds before issuing the decisive clip_qa call; a few hundred seconds of drift (as in rollout 3) can land the visual check on a completely different, unrelated scene.
open_questions: Whether a clip_qa question phrased to explicitly include 'gourd/potion/consumable slot' would have caught the 上清金葫芦 change visually, since none of the 5 rollouts tried it -- this was not empirically tested here.

Whether the reference answer intends the specific 68811-68825 consumption event (drinking 上清金葫芦) or a broader gourd-tier upgrade (e.g. 老葫芦 -> 药王葫芦 progression seen earlier at 68730s) as 'the' equipment upgrade; the exact wording of what change counts as 'the gourd upgrade' is not fully disambiguated from the DB alone.
